title: Paper-based hydrogel biosensor integrated with carbon dots for portable detection of microRNA-21 using a fluorescent diffusion area as the readout
content: The early detection of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is limited by the lack of suitable biomarkers. Circulating microRNA-21 (miR-21), a key pathogenic regulator correlated with early injury, presents a promising solution for point-of-care testing. In this work, a paper-based hydrogel biosensor that relies on fluorescent areas as the readout has been constructed for the convenient and ultrasensitive quantification of miR-21. The miR-21-responsive water-absorption hydrogel loaded with carbon dots (CDs) synthesized by sodium hyaluronate and the complementary capturing DNA (cDNA) of miR-21 is constructed for fluorescent area generation on filter paper. The miR-21 can be captured by the cDNA in a hydrogel, and the cDNA in the miR-21-cDNA duplex is cleaved by a duplex-specific nuclease. Then, the released miR-21 can be captured by other cDNA, thereby achieving signal amplification. The hydrogel was degraded via the cleavage of cDNA, and the CD-containing water was then released from the hydrogel fragments and spread uniformly on filter paper, thereby forming a distinct fluorescent region. The fluorescent area can be imaged by a smartphone and quantified via the pixel ratio of the fluorescent region to the whole paper area, which is then converted to the actual physical area. The developed biosensor demonstrates a linear response to miR-21 ranging from 1 pM to 10 nM with a detection limit of 131.25 fM. The portable sensing method exhibits portability, convenience, and high selectivity and has been applied to detect miR-21 in serum samples with satisfactory results, showing promising potential for early DKD screening.
